column3: Moses addresses his people under divine command; a remote narrative parallel.
Frames 7:128 within Moses' mission to Pharaoh and the ruin of corrupters.
Links exclusive worship with steadfast endurance.
Defines the outcome for the God-conscious and rejects earthly dominance and corruption.
Establishes Moses' commissioned confrontation with Pharaoh.
Pairs worship directed to God alone with seeking His help.
Makes patience and prayer means of seeking help, with divine nearness to the patient.
Joins truthful divine commission to the release of the Israelites.
Narrates the promised inheritance after patience and Pharaoh's destruction.
Places Moses' address to his people within remembered divine favor and bestowed rule.
Shows Pharaoh's demand for proof; contextual but not a development of the exhortation.
Pairs worship of God with God-conscious restraint.
Contrasts divine provision with the prohibition of corruption in the land.
Supplies the first sign in the Pharaoh narrative without explaining patience, land, or outcome.
Connects patient endurance with a good final abode.
Develops inherited land as fulfilled promise and reward, though in a final-garden setting.
Continues the public signs confronting Pharaoh.
Names the disciplined as inheritors, adding the inheritance motif without its conditions here.
Shows Moses' people resisting their messenger, sharpening the communal pressure behind exhortation.
Records the elite's hostile recasting of Moses' sign.
Presents patience as better than proportionate retaliation.
Places messengerly action and trust under God's granting and permission.
Makes Pharaoh's elite construe Moses as a threat to their control of the land.
Combines God-consciousness, God's spacious land, and unmeasured recompense for patience.
Directly joins perseverance with worship, provision from God, and the outcome for God-consciousness.
Shows the elite delaying Moses and mobilizing opposition.
Contrast boundary: a disastrous outcome for the warned, not positive support for 7:128's reading.
Has Moses direct his people to rely on God after faith and submission.
Continues the mobilization of expert opponents without adding the focus terms.
Reiterates patience and prayer as help; largely redundant of 2:153.
Explicitly joins the command to be patient with the outcome belonging to the God-conscious.
Shows the hired opponents' incentive and contest setting.
Contrast boundary: lists patient God-conscious qualities but adds little to the land-and-outcome claim.
Recalls Pharaoh's oppression and deliverance, supplying the prior condition of 7:128's audience.
Shows Pharaoh rewarding proximity to power; a minor counterpoint to divine agency.
Exclusive worship is relevant but lacks the focus's patience, land, and outcome relation.
God's control of provision offers only a broad agency parallel.
Affirms beautiful patience, but its mixed and contrast readings limit its added value.
Links divine warning, exclusive deity, and God-consciousness.
Models appeal to God's true judgment and seeking His help against hostile descriptions.
Makes patience preserve communal strength amid conflict and ties it to divine nearness.
Uses God's spacious land to direct believers to exclusive worship.
States success for the God-conscious without developing the focus's pathway.
Contrast-rich evidence for giving and God-consciousness; too compressed to add much.
States nearness of the garden to the God-conscious, redundant outcome imagery.
A parallel prophetic call to exclusive worship and God-consciousness, not the Moses-land argument.
Shows rival leaders urging endurance in false allegiance, a contrary use of patience.
Associates patience and right action with forgiveness and great reward, broadly redundant.
States a garden reward for the God-conscious without the focus's historical setting.
God-consciousness is present, but conflicting route evidence and brevity limit value.
Joins inheritance and God-consciousness in a final-garden context, redundant of stronger inheritance cards.
Contrast boundary: regulates cooperation and God-consciousness but does not develop 7:128's claim.
States God's ultimate inheritance of the land and its inhabitants, grounding land in divine ownership.
Connects rightful divine authority to a better outcome, but only indirectly.
Combines beautiful patience with seeking God's help under a false accusation.
Shows withdrawal from rival worship and reliance on God's mercy and provision.
Treats knowledge and distinction as gifts acknowledged before God; only a broad agency parallel.
Mentions patient gratitude amid a judgment narrative, with little direct focus overlap.
Affirms God's possession of all heavens and earth and His sufficiency as guardian.
Exclusive worship language alone does not clarify the focus's exhortation.
Contrasts God with associates in a selected-servants frame; indirect support only.
Gives exclusive worship a foundational scope, reinforcing the service dimension.
Affirms God's ownership of all heavens and earth and His decisive authority.
Links later reward to faith and God-consciousness, but adds little beyond outcome parallels.
Rejects associating partners with God; relevant to exclusive reliance but otherwise remote.
Shows patience as a better communal posture, without the focus's agency or outcome.
Shows a people replaced as inheritors, a concise parallel to transferred possession.
A prophetic summons to God-consciousness without a developed outcome relation.
Names divine favor as gift; too general for the focus.
God-consciousness and truthful testimony form only a remote ethical parallel.
Centers all command in God and delayed promise, but without the focus's patient instruction.
Pairs patience and God-consciousness against hostile plotting; a secondary conflict parallel.
Moses assigns final outcome to God's knowledge and denies success to wrongdoers.
Pairs patience with reliance on the Lord, reinforcing the disposition in 7:128.
God's independence from all on earth is a broad ownership parallel only.
Makes support conditional on patience and God-consciousness in a distinct battle setting.
Moses declares corrupt work subject to God's nullification, supporting the downfall side of the narrative.
A terse command for patience directed to the Lord; redundant of fuller patience cards.
Shows later communal self-wronging and repentance, but not the focus's promised outcome.
Shows willing patience under testing; a secondary, non-Moses parallel.
Moses warns opponents against fabricating against God and links it to failure.
Boundary evidence: endurance after judgment does not alter the settled destination.
Faith and God-consciousness amid divine testing are only a broad moral parallel.
A servant's received mercy and knowledge support dependence on God only indirectly.
A Moses-community case of arrogant wealth and wrongdoing; distant from the focus's exhortation.
False attribution and claimed assistance form only a remote help-related parallel.
Explicitly makes rule God's gift to whom He wills, clarifying divine disposal of authority.
States blessed conditions for the God-conscious, redundant final-outcome imagery.
Makes guidance God's choice among servants and warns against association; broad agency support.
Exclusive worship and God's witness offer a secondary divine-agency parallel.
Moses rejects seeking another deity after favor; contextual but later and not focused on 7:128's claim.
Places reverent fear among God's servants, only indirectly related to God-conscious outcome.
Contrasts believing servants with associating partners and their destinations; remote to the focus.
Patience is explicitly from God amid plotting, but adds little after fuller patience parallels.
No material connection to patience, land, divine help, or outcome in 7:128.
God's servants receive freedom from fear and grief; a distant service-outcome parallel.
Contrasts former worldly power with its outcome, but is tail-audit and broadly framed.
Calls for patience under the Lord's judgment and refusal of rival obedience; redundant but relevant.
Garden reward for the God-conscious repeats an already well-covered outcome motif.
God-consciousness and refusal of rival obedience offer a late, secondary boundary parallel.
The elite frame Moses and his people as a threat to their order in the land, sharpening the contested-land setting.
The believing magicians answer coercion with return to God and endurance, a direct resistance parallel.
Direct sequel: Moses couples possible destruction of the enemy with succession in the land and a test of conduct.
Shows divine retribution against Pharaoh's party after their denial, completing the adversary's downfall.
Moses directs his people toward a land assigned by God, giving a close land-and-people parallel.
Records fearful refusal before entry into the assigned land, a contrary response to 7:128's exhortation.
The consequence of refusal confines the people, showing that land-related promise is not automatic.
Makes trials the setting for the command to give good news to the patient.
Includes patience under hardship within the profile of truthful God-conscious conduct.
Places severe communal trial beside the question of divine help and the assurance of its nearness.
Pairs endurance in a smaller faithful group with God's presence for the patient.
Combines a plea for poured-out patience, firm footing, and help against hostile people.
Shows many prophetic companions enduring without yielding and associates patience with divine love.
Commands patience and God-consciousness in the face of hostile speech.
Explicitly joins patient perseverance, vigilance, and God-consciousness with success.
Places human succession in the earth under divine appointment and testing.
Recalls succession after a prior people, adding a historical pattern of divinely transferred standing.
Recalls succession in the land after a prior people and warns against corruption there.
Connects faith and God-consciousness with opened blessings, a conditional counterpart to the outcome claim.
Describes making later people successors in the earth in order to observe their conduct.
Pairs beautiful patience with seeking God's help amid a family crisis.
Explicitly joins God-consciousness and patience with preservation of reward for good-doers.
Joins patience for the Lord with a good final abode, a close outcome parallel.
Treats Moses' signs as reminders containing lessons for every patient and grateful person.
Links reliance on God with endurance under harm from opponents.
States divine nearness to the God-conscious and those who act well.
Commands steadfast companionship with servants who call on their Lord, giving a social form of patience.
Commands patient endurance before hostile speech and sustained worship.
States that the righteous inherit the earth, a direct inheritance-of-land parallel.
Describes those established in the land as maintaining worship, almsgiving, right, and restraint from wrong.
Promises believing right-doers succession in the earth and secure worship, while retaining conditions.
Makes patience the basis of elevated recompense and peace.
Names God as the one who makes successors in the earth, supporting divine disposal of land.
Promises favor to the oppressed, making them leaders and inheritors; a close parallel to 7:137 and 7:128.
Connects patient endurance with repeated reward and repelling evil with good.
Qualifies God's better reward by faith, right action, and patient endurance.
Commands patience on the basis that God's promise is true.
Links patient certainty with divinely appointed leaders who guide by God's command.
Describes inheritance of land, homes, and property after displacement of opponents.
Calls humans successors in the earth while locating denial's consequence with God.
Affirms divine support for messengers and believers in worldly life and at testimony.
Commands patience because God's promise is true, within a Moses-Pharaoh discourse context.
Repeats the command to patience and the truth of God's promise amid messengerly opposition.
Reserves a high moral response for those who are patient, extending patience beyond retaliation.
Commends patient endurance and forgiveness as matters of resolute determination.
Commands messengerly patience after the resolute messengers, in a warning-and-outcome frame.
Promises divine help to those who aid God's cause and firmness of footing.
Makes God-consciousness the condition for a divinely made way out.
Pairs provision beyond expectation with reliance on God and His sufficiency.
Makes patience the basis of garden reward and protection.
